title: Fee cuts for retirees moving to tax-free income: 'Significant changes'
full_text:
A major superannuation fund with more than a million members is giving a boost to older Australians switching over to retirement. Members over the age of 60 will face lower costs when drawing down on their nest egg under new fee changes for account holders, HESTA says.
The Australian super industry is gearing up for a wave of retirements, with funds in a race to improve their member options with new pension bonuses and specialised income products being rolled out. With the compulsory superannuation system at the centre of political debate at the moment, fees have also been in the spotlight.
Today, HESTA announced it is reducing admin fees on income stream accounts, as well as lowering the minimum balance requirement for retired members to start one.

For about half of Aussies who don't take a lump sum payment of their superannuation, income stream accounts provide a regular tax-free income from their super nest egg.
The fixed administration fee for all of HESTA's retirement products will be reduced by more than 16 per cent to $65 per annum, while the asset-based fee will be cut from 0.23 per cent to 0.18 per cent per annum.
The change means a retiree with a $50,000 balance will see the total of these two fees fall by more than 18 per cent, to $170 a year, HESTA says.
The fund, which is home to more than a million members and has over $108 billion in assets, is also effectively scrapping the current $10,000 minimum balance for starting an Income Stream account, with just a $250 balance soon needed to process pension payments.
The changes will come into effect from September 30.
"These are significant changes for our members in, or about to enter, retirement," HESTA CEO Debby Blakey said.
"We understand the challenges many Australians face in retirement and it's terrific to be able to deliver lower fees at a time when persistent inflation is driving cost-of-living pressures.
"We are also pleased to be able to offer income stream accounts to even more members, so they have the opportunity to take advantage of tax-free investment returns."
HESTA is also advocating for a key rule change, as part of a push to modernise the retirement system, to allow the ability for retirees to top-up income stream accounts from working.
While speaking to Yahoo Finance earlier this month, Blakey also advocated for reform around the Age Pension and the current income test taper rate that can see pensioners who work face an effective tax rate as high as 70 per cent.
author: Nick Whigham
heading: Superannuation and Investments
